Collective Worship
Winsley is a Church of England school. The school was provided by the local parish church of St Nicholas and continues to work in partnership with the church and with the Diocese of Salisbury.
Being a school with a Christian Ethos means that we:
In practice, this means (among other things) that our Collective Worship will often be based on a Bible story or Christian principle; the main Christian festivals will be celebrated (often with a special service at St Nicholas), and children will be encouraged to explore what part faith might play in their lives.
We encourage all our children to be spiritually inquisitive, empowering them to make informed choices that will enhance their ability to achieve lifelong success and fulfilment as set out in the School Vision.
Our identity as a Church of England school is central to the character and vision of the school and therefore we will always aim to do justice to our Christian foundation.
As an inclusive school, however, we encourage our children to respect the views and beliefs of each individual. Our RE curriculum develops a breadth of experience and understanding of all world faiths and we aim to ensure that all children have an informed and tolerant view of cultural diversity. This is expressed in our Equality policy. Should they wish, parents can arrange to withdraw their child(ren) from RE lessons and Collective Worship.

Church School
Winsley Primary School is proud to be a Church School and works closely with both the Diocese of Salisbury and our local church (St Nicholas) for the greater good of our local community and further afield. Everyone is welcome in our school, regardless of whether you or your child have a faith or identify as being a Christian or not. In our school we have multiple faiths and beliefs which are celebrated!
Vision & Values
The conviction at the heart of our vision is that all who are part of our school community formed around our vision will discover an education that embraces excellence and academic rigour within the wider framework of spiritual, physical, intellectual, emotional, moral and social development and enables us all to flourish.
Vision Statement
Our vision is to be an exceptional church school committed to investing in young lives. A school where staff and governors work in partnership with parents to provide a caring, stimulating environment rooted in Christian values; a school with high expectations where all are valued and nurtured as individuals because they are uniquely created and loved by God.
Collective Worship at Winsley CofE Primary School
Collective Worship
Full guidance can be found here: Church of England sets out guidance for collective worship | The Church of England
As a school we work with our local vicar and other church members to plan and deliver acts of worship that are invitational, reflective and engaging. There is plenty of flexibility in the provision of collective worship to enable all pupils to benefit without compromising their beliefs.
Collective worship gives pupils and school staff the opportunity to:
Our collective worships are planned together with the children, Rev Tessa and our worshsip ambassadors.
Engage in an act of community.
Express praise and thanksgiving to God.
Be still and reflect.
Foster respect and deepen spiritual awareness.
Affirm Christian values and attitudes.
Share each other's joys and challenges.
Celebrate special times in the Christian calendar.
A Typical Week Looks Like:
Spirituality At Winsley Primary School:
The Winsley Vision Narrative
Winsley Vision Narrative
‘Some seed fell on the good earth and produced a harvest beyond his wildest dreams.’Matthew 13:8
This image, reminiscent of the parable of the sower, represents the vision of Winsley CofE Primary School. A farm represents the school and local rural community while the Light of God shines in the form of the sun providing essential energy to allow all to grow and flourish.
The successive fields represent the children progressing from EYFS where the ploughed field provides a rich foundation followed by sown seeds, to the roots and shoots leading to corn growing strong, then sheaves of harvested corn finally being prepared to be taken by tractor-trailer from Year 6 to the next destination, which is secondary school. The journey of the harvest is accompanied by Jesus in the form of the canal that flows constantly alongside.
A hot-air balloon, tethered to a good ground, is occupied by the headteacher overseeing the school community, the governors providing a stabilising influence and the Diocese and the MAT partnership delivering security and direction. The three school values are represented by the three stripes of the balloon by which the whole school community is guided.
Various aspects of our educational journey are represented in the thorny bushes where we sometimes are stuck, the significant presence of St Nicholas Church, which offers inspiration and support, and a stone wall spanning all fields that indicate that we are stronger together.
Our vision is to ensure that everyone in our school community has the opportunity to flourish spiritually, academically, socially and morally inline with our school values of: Kindness, Courage and Wisdom.
The Palladian Academy Trust Group Of Schools
We are part of an academy of 13 schools known as the Palladian Academy Trust. There are 5 church schools
Winsley Church of England Primary School
Combe Down Church of England Primary School
St Philips Church of England Primary School,
Westbury Leigh Church of England Primary School
Widcombe Infant School
Widcombe Church of England Junior School
Oldfield Park Infant School
Oldfield Park Junior School
Westwood with Iford Primary School
Churchfields, The Village School
Fitzmaurice Primary School
St Martins Garden School
Ralph Allen School - our only Trust secondary school which, together we fall under the diocese of Bath & Wells and Salisbury.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome to Winsley C of E Primary School - Winsley Primary School
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Winsley C of E Primary School
To be the Headteacher at Winsley Church of England Primary School is a privilege and one I am very proud of and grateful for.
In the time I have been here, I have witnessed so much kindness and energy amongst the pupils, staff and community. It is clear that the three core values of ‘Wisdom, Kindness and Courage’ are abundant and are the foundation for all learning.
Based on the Parable of the Sower, it is our aspiration that our school be the ‘good earth’ for all our stakeholders: to always provide an environment that will enable everyone in our community, irrespective of circumstance, to thrive.
I have a very strong team of teaching and support staff in all areas of the school and our governors and the local church care deeply about the school. We are proud to be members of ‘The Palladian Multi-Academy Trust’ and look forward to developing alongside fellow schools in the trust.
Our curriculum recognises children’s prior learning and life experiences; provides opportunities to build on their cultural capital; develops children’s social and communication skills and builds resilience in order to become creative, critical thinkers.
I warmly welcome you to our school family and look forward to working with you and your child to help them aspire to be whatever they want to be.

pageCache.pageTitle: Wraparound Care and opening hours - Winsley Primary School
pageCache.text:
Wraparound Care and opening hours
Compulsory opening hours
The school's compulsory hours are:
Monday - Friday 8:45am - 3:15pm (32.5 hours).
As per the September 2022 guidance from DfE.
We offer wraparound care in the form of Breakfast and After School Club. The clubs are a fun, safe environment where Winsley children can still learn, play and interact with adults they know and trust. Everybody is welcome, from Reception to Year 6 with a range of different activities to suit the different age groups. During wraparound care, the children have access to safe and fun play equipment and daily planned activities, but also have the ability to choose what suits them.Wraparound Care offers regular and ad-hoc care both before and after school as follows:
Breakfast Club – 7.30-8.40am, £5.70 per session
The children have a range of activities to do. They are offered toast or cereal for their breakfast with a drink. This is a relaxed environment ready to start the school day.
After School Club – We run 3 sessions:
3.15pm - 4.15pm - £ 4.00 per session
4.15pm - 6.00pm - £ 7.85 per session
3.15pm - 6.00pm - £ 11.85 per session
Children may partake in a range of activites of their choice, whether it be art and crafts, playing outisde, supervised PE, board games and much, much more. The children have the choice to stay within KS1 and KS2 groups or join in with everyone.
Children enjoy a light supper at After School Club, please see the attachtment below with example food they will be offered. Full Menu
How to book
Bookings must be made 48 hours in advance via Arbor. We understand that sometimes urgent last minute bookings are sometimes needed and therefore please contact the school office on 01225 863365 or email wpsadmin@palladianacademytrust.com if this is the case.
Please read all additional paperwork for terms & conditions. All new children to wraparound care will be required to fill out the initial booking forms.
If you are unsure how to use Arbor, click here to open the Arbor website and instructions on how to book.
We also accept childcare vouchers!

Uniform policy
Uniform is compulsory at Winsley Primary School.
All items of clothing including: coats, shoes and PE kit must be clearly named.
At Winsley Primary School we are proud to be a part of our amazing community and we wear our school uniform with pride; we have shared high standards and expectations necessary to prepare our children for their future.
The colours of the Winsley Primary School uniform are grey and black. We thank our families for supporting us in maintaining our shared high standard of the presentation of our children.
As a school we understand that many of our families face difficult financial choices, we have worked very hard to ensure our uniforms are affordable, hard wearing and “use competitive and transparent contracts with suppliers” as required by the Department of Education. All of the items listed below are required.
All children must have:
A sensible coat of the appropriate thickness for the weather, with hood, preferably a plain dark colour.
All children must have a pair of wellingtons for outdoor play.
All children must have a pair of slippers. These should be appropriate to walk in and be covered over the toe and have a back. Flip flops or sliders are not appropriate. Crocs are accepted with the back strap securely fastened when worn.
All children must have a book bag or a suitable ruck sack that can be hung on their peg to carry their school reading book and reading diary to and from school in.
Children in Key Stage One must have a drawstring bag that can be kept on their peg with spare clothes in. These do not have to be uniform. Please include underwear and socks.
Earrings, jewellery, hairstyles, nail polish and tattoos:
Children may wear a wristwatch but are not permitted to wear necklaces, rings, charity wristbands or bracelets of any description. These will be removed in school and we cannot guarantee or be responsible for their safe keeping.
In the interests of Health and Safety, we prefer the children not to wear earrings. Only 1 pair of plain studs may be worn in the ear lobe only, one in each ear. These must be removed or taped up for PE.
If your children are having their ears pierced, please consider to do this in a long school holiday so correct aftercare can take place.
Hair longer than shoulder length must be tied back at all times. Any hair bands must be subtle and not distracting.
Children are not allowed to have extreme hairstyles. For example, mohicans, extreme dyed or highlighted hair. For Health and Safety reasons, hair below shoulder length should be tied back securely and long fringes clipped back (boys and girls) and be off the face so that eye contact can be made.
Children must not wear nail polish, false nails, makeup or tattoos, including Henna.
All of the clothes below can be 'generic', they do not have to have the school logo on them as long as there is no other logo on them.
Grey jumper with logo ordered via:Scholars Uniform Shop
Grey cardigan/ jumper with logo ordered via:Scholars Uniform Shop

White polo shirt - all year
Black shorts (which are long enough to reach your fingertips when hands are by your side) or trousers - all year
Black skirt or pinafore or trousers or shorts (which are long enough to reach your fingertips when hands are by your side) - all year
Red & white check dress for summer & white socks (ankle or knee high) - all year
Black socks - all year
Black tights or socks - all year
Plain black shoes or trainers - all year
Plain black shoes or trainers - all year
Black outdoor shoes can double up as your child's PE trainers but must be plain black, smart and have no branding or any other colours
Black outdoor shoes can double up as your child's PE trainers but must be plain black, smart and have branding or any other colours
PE for Boys and Girls
PE T Shirt in house colour: Red - Autumn House / Blue - Winter House / Green - Spring House / Yellow - Summer House. These logo coloured t shirts can be ordered via Scholars Uniform Shop or you can purchase plain ones from any store. Scholars Uniform shop
Black pair of shorts (which are long enough to reach your fingertips when hands are by your side,) black jogging bottoms, black leggings or a black skort.
Black outdoor trainers (these can double up as your child’s school shoes but must be plain black and have no branding or any other colours) - all year
PE kit should be worn to school on the day that your child has this subject. Children will typically have PE twice a week. Children in key stage two also participate in swimming lessons.
In line with current DfE guidance our PTA (WISCA) runs a second-hand uniform shop. Donations of good quality clothing are always welcome, particularly plimsolls and football boots. If you are struggling to afford the second-hand uniform, please make us aware so that we can help.
Religious and Cultural Clothing
We endeavour to allow most religious requirements to be met. Parents’ requests regarding religious and cultural clothing are dealt with on a case-by-case basis by the Headteacher in consultation with the Trust.

The Winsley Curriculum
At Winsley Primary School we follow the National Curriculum as published here:
The Winsley Curriculum can be found here: WPS 2023 curriciulum.docx
At Winsley CofE Primary School we aim to deliver our innovative curriculum in the most memorable, exciting and effective way possible where high standards are always sought and attention is always given to motivating children to be lifelong learners.
We have carefully considered the needs of the children in our community so that we can correctly support them to be confident, independent and successful learners ready for the next stage in their education as responsible citizens.
We aim to teach and develop our children’s skills and knowledge across the curriculum and enhance their enjoyment through offering a range of theme days, enrichment opportunities, visits and visitors throughout the year.
We maintain a sharp focus on the core subjects of English and Maths whilst ensuring our children benefit from our engaging and carefully chosen schemes of work across the subjects. Where possible, links are made to deepen children’s understanding whilst maintaining the integrity of the curriculum.â€¯
There is a wealth of information regarding our whole school curriculum on the subject specific pages (currently under development – September 2022). Our class curriculum webs provide a deeper insight into how we work creatively to link the core and foundation subjectsâ€¯to enhance, deepenâ€¯and excite learning.
Our rich and comprehensive curriculum, tailored to our diverse community, ensures our children have the skills and qualities to meet the demands of the next phase of their education and that they are confident and inquisitive learners able to develop a deep understanding of the world around them.â€¯
English, Maths, Science and RSE are taught to each year group specifically within our mixed age classes.
Across Key Stage One we follow a two year rolling programme of study for: History, Geography, Art, DT, RE, Music, Computing, PSHE and PE. We have a clear progression of skills for each year group to ensure children are supported and challenged accordingly.
English, Maths, Science, Computing and PSHE (including RSE) skills are taught to each year group within our mixed age classes .
Across Key Stage Two we follow a four year rolling programme of study for History, Geography, Art, DT, RE, Music, MFL and PE. We have a clear progression of skills for each year group to ensure children are supported and challenged accordingly.
From September 2022 we use the Little Wandle approach to teach phonics.
Training videos to help parents and families can be found here.
Or teaching is based on the National Curriculum; which we have mapped out below showing how we intend to cover all the areas. Due to mixed age groups we have a 2 year curriculum cycle in Key Stage 1 and a 4 year cycle in Key Stage 2.
